## Summary

Fixes #84

crates.io's newest `lino-objects-codec` is 0.9.3, which requires `links-notation ^0.27.1`, although `main` moved to 0.31.x in #82. Merging this PR publishes **0.9.4** with `links-notation ^0.31.4` (the latest release, published 2026-11-14). Every later release also checks that the crates.io artifact matches the source.

### Root cause

The push that merged #82 started [Rust CI/CD run 42662099641](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/actions/runs/42662099641). Lint and the Ubuntu and Windows tests passed. **Test (Rust on macos-15)** was cancelled with no steps, and its annotation says:

> The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts

`build` requires every test leg to succeed, and `auto-release` requires `build`, so both were skipped. The patch fragment `rust/changelog.d/20261109_120000_issue_81_links_notation_0_31_3.md` stayed unreleased on `main`. The next commit on `main` didn't touch `rust/`, so nothing triggered the release again, and the red run never said that a crates.io release was owed.

Re-uploading 0.9.3 isn't possible because crates.io versions are immutable. The fix has to be a new version.

### Changes

1. **New crate version.** This PR adds a patch fragment (`rust/changelog.d/20261114_120000_issue_84_publish_links_notation_0_31.md`) and touches `rust/**`, so Auto Release runs on the merge commit. It collects both pending patch fragments, bumps `rust/Cargo.toml` from 0.9.3 to 0.9.4, publishes it, and creates the `rust_v0.9.4` tag and GitHub release.
   - The version isn't edited by hand because `check-version-modification.mjs` rejects manual version changes in PRs. The fragment is this repository's release trigger.
2. **Latest parser.** `links-notation` 0.31.4 came out after the issue was filed, and the dependency freshness gate fails PRs on outdated direct dependencies. So, following #81:
   - Rust 0.31.4, including the four experiment crates and their lockfiles
   - JS `^0.31.4`
   - Python `>=0.31.4,<0.32.0`
   - C# stays on 0.31.1, which is the latest on NuGet
   - Refreshed tool pins: ESLint 10.15.0, Prettier 3.10.1, Ruff 0.17.5, `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` 18.12.0, `peter-evans/create-pull-request` v8.1.3 (hash pin)
   - JS, Python and C# get patch fragments too (the C# one covers the test SDK refresh, which the C# Changeset Check requires).
3. **Post-publish check of the registry metadata.** Both release jobs run the new `rust/scripts/verify-published-crate.mjs --consumer`, after the GitHub release is created. It:
   - reads `GET /api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>/dependencies` and compares every normal, dev and build dependency with `Cargo.toml`. The requirement must match (the manifest's `0.31.4` is stored as `^0.31.4`), the `optional` flag must match, and nothing may be missing or extra;
   - builds a fresh consumer crate with `lino-objects-codec = "=<version>"` from crates.io. The consumer round-trips an object through `encode`/`decode`, and `cargo tree` must resolve each normal dependency to a version that meets the manifest requirement. This is the issue's reproduction, run against the real artifact.
4. **Release Pending Check job.** It runs on pushes to `main` when Test or Build Package didn't succeed. If changelog fragments are still unreleased, it fails with an error that:
   - lists the fragments;
   - points to "Re-run failed jobs" when the failure was infrastructure;
   - otherwise gives `gh workflow run rust.yml --ref main -f release_mode=instant -f bump_type=patch`.
5. **Case study** in `docs/case-studies/issue-84/README.md`, and a reproduction script in `experiments/issue-84/`.

### How to reproduce

```sh
bash experiments/issue-84/reproduce.sh 0.9.3
# ::error title=Published crate differs from the source::lino-objects-codec@0.9.3 on crates.io does not match Cargo.toml
#   - links-notation (normal): crates.io has ^0.27.1, expected ^0.31.4
```

When the same script is given the 0.9.3 manifest, it passes. The consumer resolves `links-notation v0.27.1` and round-trips, so the check accepts a correct release. Logs: `experiments/issue-84/verify-0.9.3-*.log`.

### Tests

- **Round trips and conformance:** `cargo test --all-features` passes against `links-notation` 0.31.4. That includes the shared `fixtures/` conformance suites, compact interop, indented multiline, documented examples and the proptest JSON bridge.
- **Other languages against the new pins:** JS `npm test` + lint, Python `pytest` (536 passed) + ruff + mypy, and C# `dotnet test` (541 passed) all pass.
- **New unit tests** in `rust/scripts/crates-release-helpers.test.mjs`, run by the Lint job, cover:
  - manifest parsing, including `[[example]]` and target tables;
  - requirement normalization;
  - the real 0.9.3 registry answer being flagged;
  - missing, extra and `optional` mismatches;
  - fail-closed responses;
  - caret semantics for 0.x versions;
  - `cargo tree` parsing.
- **Workflow checks:**
  - `actionlint` 1.7.12 (Docker image with shellcheck) and `zizmor` 1.32.0 (regular and pedantic passes) report nothing;
  - `scripts/check_dependency_freshness.py` passes;
  - `check-links-notation-parity.mjs` passes.

### After merge

The publication can only happen on `main` after merge, so it can't be verified inside this PR. On the merge run, the last step of Auto Release prints the dependencies crates.io serves for 0.9.4 and the `links-notation` version a fresh consumer resolves. If the macOS runner isn't acquired again, the Release Pending Check job explains how to finish the release.
title: Publish the Rust links-notation 0.31 migration as 0.9.4 and verify the registry artifact

## Summary

Fixes #81

`encode`/`encodeLine` wrote a finite integer Number beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` as plain digits, and `decode`/`decodeLine` read those digits back as a string:

```js
const value = { count: 1e18, nested: [-9007199254740992] };
decode({ notation: encode({ obj: value }) });
// before: { count: '1000000000000000000', nested: ['-9007199254740992'] }
// after:  { count: 1000000000000000000, nested: [-9007199254740992] }
```

### Root cause

- `formatNumber` in `js/src/readable.js` returned `String(value)`. For an integer Number from `2 ** 53` up to `1e21` that's a plain digit string. (From `1e21` on, `String` already uses an exponent.)
- `refToValue` deliberately reads bare digits that don't fit a safe integer as a string, so a `bigint` or a long identifier keeps every digit.
- So the writer and the reader disagreed for unsafe integer Numbers.

### Fix

As the issue suggested, after the existing special-number handling `formatNumber` writes an integer Number that isn't a safe integer with `value.toExponential()`. Called with no argument, `toExponential` keeps exactly the digits needed to identify the double, so the reader's float branch gives back the same Number.

| Number | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `9007199254740991` (max safe) | `9007199254740991` | `9007199254740991` |
| `9007199254740992` | `9007199254740992` | `9.007199254740992e+15` |
| `-9007199254740992` | `-9007199254740992` | `-9.007199254740992e+15` |
| `1e18` | `1000000000000000000` | `1e+18` |
| `1000000000000000100` (the double `1e18 + 128`) | `1000000000000000100` | `1.0000000000000001e+18` |
| `1e21` and above | `1e+21` | `1e+21` (unchanged) |

These stay the same:
- Safe integers keep their plain digits.
- Numeric-looking strings stay quoted (`"1e+18"`, `"1000000000000000000"`), so they stay strings.
- Object keys stay strings, including numeric-looking ones.
- A `bigint` is still written as its digits, and an unsafe one still reads back as its exact digit string.
- The reader isn't touched, so documents written by earlier versions decode exactly as before.
- The compact format already kept the Number type, and a test now checks that too.

The Python, Rust and C# readable writers don't have this problem. From reading their code, they always keep a decimal point or an exponent on a float (`repr`, `{:?}`, and `ToString("R")` plus `.0`), so their readers never see a float as an integer. The shared cross-language fixtures (`fixtures/readable-format/cases.json`) aren't changed: no existing case is an unsafe integer.

Docs: `README.md`, `js/README.md` and the `readable.js` header describe the new rule. I added a patch changeset in `js/.changeset/issue-81-unsafe-integer-numbers.md`.

### Reproduce

```sh
cd js && npm ci && cd ..
node experiments/issue-81/reproduce.mjs
```

Before the fix, both forms print `FAIL` and the script exits with 1. After it, both print `ok` and it exits with 0. `experiments/issue-81/README.md` has the notes.

### Tests

`js/tests/test_unsafe_integer_numbers.test.js` covers the readable (`encode`/`decode`) and single-line (`encodeLine`/`decodeLine`) forms:
- positive and negative unsafe integer Numbers (`±(2^53)`, `±(2^53 + 2)`, `±1e18`, `1000000000000000100`, `2^64`, `1e21`, `Number.MAX_VALUE`)
- the safe boundaries `±Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and other safe integers, which keep their plain digits
- matching strings and numeric-looking keys, which keep their type and spelling
- unsafe integers inside nested arrays and objects, and the exact case from the issue
- `bigint` semantics, and that bare unsafe digits written by hand still read as strings
- the compact round trip

Against the old `formatNumber`, 24 of the 49 new tests fail. With the fix, all 49 pass, the full JS suite passes (597/597), and `npm run check` (eslint, prettier, jscpd) passes.

### CI housekeeping

The Dependency Freshness gate already failed on this branch's first commit, before any change: new releases had come out. To clear it:
- I moved `links-notation` from 0.27.1 to 0.31.x in all four packages. That's 0.31.3 on npm, PyPI and crates.io, including the four experiment crates, and 0.31.1 on NuGet, the latest release there. The parser-version gate compares only major.minor, so all four still pin 0.31.x.
- I refreshed jscpd 5.4.3, the npm and Cargo lockfiles, ruff 0.17.4, scriv 1.8.1 and xunit.v3 4.0.3.
- I bumped `peter-evans/create-pull-request` to v8.1.2 (hash-pinned), `zizmor-action` to v0.8.1 and zizmor to 1.32.0.
- Each language has a changelog entry for the bump.

Every suite passed locally against the new parser:
- JS: 597/597, plus `npm run check`
- Python: 536 passed; ruff and mypy are clean
- Rust: `cargo test --all-features` passed
- C#: `dotnet test` passed

`scripts/check_dependency_freshness.py`, `scripts/check-links-notation-parity.mjs` and `npm outdated` all passed locally too.

### [skip-parity]

Only the JavaScript source changes. The bug comes from JavaScript having a single `Number` type, where an integer double and an integer share one spelling. Python (`repr`), Rust (`{:?}`) and C# (`ToString("R")`, plus `.0` when needed) always write a float with a decimal point or an exponent, so their readers already get a float back. The shared fixtures don't change.
title: fix(js): keep unsafe integer Numbers as Numbers in readable formats

body:
## Summary

Fixes #79

In a browser bundle (Vite, esbuild, Rollup) there is no `process` and no `Buffer`. `parseIndented`, `decode` and every other parse threw `ReferenceError: process is not defined`, and decoding legacy `(base64 "…")` values or the compact format needed `Buffer`.

### Root cause

- `js/src/debug.js`: `isDebugEnabled()` read `process.env.LINO_CODEC_DEBUG` unguarded, and every parse calls `trace()` → `isDebugEnabled()`. `trace()` also wrote to `process.stderr` directly.
- `js/src/readable.js` (`decodeMarkedValue`, `(base64 "…")`) and `js/src/codec.js` (compact encode/decode) used `Buffer.from(…, 'base64')`.

### Fix

- `debug.js` looks up `globalThis.process` safely. Without it, `LINO_CODEC_DEBUG` counts as unset (tracing off unless `setDebugEnabled(true)`), and trace lines go to `console.debug` when there is no `process.stderr`. Node behavior is unchanged.
- New `js/src/base64.js`: UTF-8 base64 that uses `Buffer` when it exists and otherwise `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` plus a small pure-JS base64 codec. I didn't use `atob` because it throws on input that `Buffer` accepts. The fallback decoder follows `Buffer`'s lenient rules (accepts both the `+/` and `-_` alphabets, skips other characters, stops at the first `=`, drops leftover bits, keeps a leading BOM), so the same document decodes to the same string in Node and in a browser.
- Documented the browser behavior in `README.md` and `js/README.md`; added a patch changeset.

### Reproduce

```sh
cd js && npm ci && cd ..
node experiments/issue-79/reproduce.mjs
```

The script deletes `globalThis.process` and `globalThis.Buffer` and then loads the codec. Before the fix, `parseIndented`, `decode` and the `(base64 "…")` decode failed with `process is not defined`. After the fix, every case prints `ok`.

`experiments/issue-79/browser.html` runs the same cases in a real browser without a bundler. In Chromium (Playwright) it reported `typeof process: undefined, typeof Buffer: undefined` and `ok` for all six cases: formatIndented, parseIndented, decode, `(base64 "…")` decode, compact round trip with Unicode, and parseIndented with tracing on.

### Tests

`js/tests/test_browser_globals.test.js` deletes both globals before loading the library. `node --test` runs each file in its own process. The test covers:
- `formatIndented`/`parseIndented`/`decode` without `process`; `isDebugEnabled()` is `false` without an environment;
- `(base64 "…")` decode and a compact round trip with Unicode without `Buffer`, where the compact output must match the `Buffer` path exactly;
- tracing falls back to `console.debug`;
- the fallback base64 encoder and decoder match `Buffer` byte for byte on fixed edge cases and 500 generated inputs.

Before the fix, 6 of the 9 tests fail. After it, the full JS suite passes (548/548), and `npm run check` (eslint, prettier, jscpd) passes.

### CI housekeeping

- Bumped `eslint` to `^10.14.0` and refreshed `js/package-lock.json`. The Dependency Freshness gate failed because a new release had come out; that is unrelated to this change.

### [skip-parity]

This change applies only to JavaScript. The bug comes from JavaScript runtimes that lack the Node globals `process`/`Buffer`. Python (`os.environ`, `base64`), Rust (`std::env::var`, which returns `Err` on targets without an environment) and C# (`Environment`, `Convert`) read the environment and base64 through their standard libraries and have no equivalent failure. The encoded output is unchanged, so the four implementations stay byte-for-byte compatible.
title: fix(js): run parseIndented/decode without process and Buffer globals (browser)

`formatIndented({ id: 'doc', obj: { t: 'line1\nline2' } })` produces readable text that `parseIndented` previously rejected with `Unterminated quoted reference`. Quoted multiline values now round-trip without losing newlines, blank lines, indentation, quotes, or carriage returns.

Fixes #77

## Changes

- JavaScript splits definitions at newlines outside quoted references. It preserves quoted continuations in object values, nested definitions, arrays, keys, and identifiers. Literal backticks and empty references are quoted so they also round-trip.
- Python, Rust, and C# retain the body verbatim before passing it to links-notation. Their former blank-line filtering silently deleted content inside quoted values; Rust's `lines()` also stripped carriage returns from CRLF values.
- All four parsers expose counts through the existing, disabled-by-default `LINO_CODEC_DEBUG` trace switch.
- All four packages have patch release fragments. The Python pytest/Ruff/mypy development floors are refreshed because the dependency freshness gate rejected their previous floors.

The existing single-line representation, legacy headers, dynamic scalar parsing in JavaScript, and existing null handling in the other implementations remain covered by their original tests.

## Reproduce and verify

From the repository root after installing JavaScript dependencies:

```sh
node experiments/issue-77/reproduce.mjs
node --test js/tests/test_indented_multiline.test.js
node js/examples/multiline_catalog.js
```

Before the fix, the reproduction fails all six samples. The new JavaScript suite fails 20 of 23 tests on the original code; the new Python suite fails 5 of 18 cases; Rust and C# both fail the blank-continuation fixture. All pass with the fix.

The shared [18-case fixture](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/blob/issue-77-648feda2cbaf/fixtures/indented-format/strings.json) is exercised by automated regression tests in every language. JavaScript additionally tests all 2,380 strings of length 0–3 from a 13-character alphabet, nested definitions/arrays, multiline keys/identifiers, all supported quote kinds, legacy headers, and malformed input.

[Investigation and regression evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/blob/issue-77-648feda2cbaf/experiments/issue-77/README.md).

## Local validation

| Implementation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript | 539 tests; 13 release-helper tests; ESLint, Prettier, duplication check and examples pass |
| Python | 536 tests; Ruff lint/format, mypy and file-size check pass |
| Rust | All-feature suite: 128 tests including doctests; no-default-feature suite, clippy with `-D warnings`, fmt, file-size check and 22 release-helper tests pass |
| C# | 541 tests; Release build with warnings as errors and format verification pass |
| Shared checks | 44 Node tests, 12 Python tests, language/parser parity, all four release-fragment validators and all 140 direct dependency declarations pass |

Rust builds ran with one job and debug information disabled to stay within the container's memory limit. No functionality was removed.

## CI validation

Current-head results are available in the [pull request checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/pull/78/checks). All four language pipelines, cross-language and parser-version parity, shared scripts, dependency freshness, security scans, workflow linting, and documentation links are required for completion.
title: Fix multiline string round-trips in indented parsers
